title: Normalized quotient-diagram adjunction and exchange identities
statement: For two small sites, a geometric morphism with its canonical constant coefficient lift, a commutative Noetherian ring A and ideal I [def-pur-adic-site-strict-quotient-interface], there exist the actual quotient-diagram presentation p [def-pur-perfect-quotient-exchange-presentation] and common-composite isomorphism d from restricted quotient direct image to direct image of strict restriction. PresentationNormalized holds, d is its prescribed restrictionMate, restriction of exchange followed by d equals strictExchange on the entire strict tower, finiteExchange is the fixed finiteProjection, and the displayed evaluation/restriction square of the parent theorem commutes at each positive level. This assertion has no perfectness hypothesis and asserts no projection invertibility or completion-unit identity.

proof.text: Construct the two strict diagonal presentations and their normalized reductions. Lift the actual component inverse images to semilinear quotient systems, assemble their component adjunctions, and transport through the sequence-site equivalences. Evaluation of extension sends each pure tensor to itself; scalar restriction keeps sections unchanged. Descend on entire flat-term K-flat representatives, retaining all quotient transitions.

Constant inverse image identifies the quotient algebra diagrams, including transitions. Use the canonical $d$ from the diagram restriction lemma and $b$ from the pullback-extension coherence lemma. The restriction-counit identity gives $(d_NU(t))^\flat=U(t^\flat)b_M$: compose it with $GU(t)$ and use naturality of $b$.

Set $M=\mathcal R_Y(PF)$, $N=\mathcal R_XF$, $t=h_F$. The representative-normalized reduction comparison and the new coherence square identify its restricted transpose with $(\Delta\varepsilon_F\otimes1)\theta_{\Delta PF}$. Since $\varepsilon^JG(\chi_F)=\Delta\varepsilon_F$, the augmented projection lemma gives exactly this transpose for $h_F^A$. Injectivity of adjunction therefore gives $dU(h_F)=h_F^A$.

proof.text: The new evaluation-adjunction lemma sends $h_F$ to the quotient-linear mate $h_{F,n}$ with the stated source and target: use quotient projection evaluation with $H=F,K=\underline A$; the two tensor-unit projections are identities. Its evaluation/restriction square identifies $U(h_{F,n})$ with $\operatorname{ev}_n(h_F^A)$ by Step 2. The augmented projection lemma identifies the latter with the ordinary counit-tensor projection. All these identifications retain the actual coefficient restrictions.

lean.statement:
theorem quotientExchangeDiagramNormalization [IsNoetherianRing A] :
    ∃ (p : Presentation f A I)
      (d : p.push.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙ p.atY.restrictionD ≅
        p.atX.restrictionD ⋙ f.towerPush A),
      PresentationNormalized f A I p ∧
      d.hom = restrictionMate p ∧
      (∀ F : X.derived A,
        p.atY.restrictionD.map ((exchange p).app F) ≫
            d.hom.app (p.atX.reductionD.obj F) = (strictExchange p).app F) ∧
      (∀ (F : X.derived A) (n : ℕ),
        (finiteExchange p n).app F = f.finiteProjection A I n F) ∧
      (∀ (F : X.derived A) (n : ℕ),
        (Y.evaluate A n).map ((strictExchange p).app F) ≫
            (Y.evaluate A n).map
              ((f.towerPush A).map (p.reductionX.tower.hom.app F)) ≫
            (f.evaluatePushIso A n).hom.app ((X.reduction A I).obj F) ≫
            (f.push A).map ((X.finiteEvaluationIso A I n).hom.app F) ≫
            (f.finiteRestrictionPushIso A I n).hom.app ((X.finiteReduction A I n).obj F) =
          (Y.evaluate A n).map (p.reductionY.tower.hom.app ((f.push A).obj F)) ≫
            (Y.finiteEvaluationIso A I n).hom.app ((f.push A).obj F) ≫
            (Y.finiteRestriction A I n).map ((finiteExchange p n).app F))
